profile.summary: Prosit is a neural network that predicts the MS2 fragment intensities and the indexed retention time (iRT) of a peptide. The input is a list of peptide sequence, precursor charge and collision energy; the output is a predicted spectrum, written as a MaxQuant style msms.txt, an msp library or a generic text file. It is used to build spectral libraries and to rescore peptide-spectrum matches. The original implementation runs as a server in a Docker container and needs a CUDA GPU.
profile.summary_source_locator: README: Prosit, Usage, Using Prosit on your data, Hardware

summary_quotes.text: Prosit is a deep neural network to predict iRT values and MS2 spectra for given peptide sequences.
Send any list of (Peptide, Precursor charge, Collision energy) in the format of `/example/peptidelist.csv` to a running instance of the Prosit server.
Currently two output formats are supported: a MaxQuant style `msms.txt` not including the iRT value and a generic text file (that works with Spectronaut)

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Two models are loaded side by side: one for fragment intensities and one for iRT. A peptide is encoded over an alphabet of the 20 common amino acids plus oxidised methionine, so 21 symbols, with cysteine always treated as carbamidomethylated. The intensity model covers y and b ions up to fragment charge 3, with no loss, water loss and ammonia loss variants, for up to 29 cleavage positions. Prediction runs behind an HTTP server: a posted peptide list is converted to numpy arrays, both models predict, and the result is written in the requested output format.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: This repository is marked deprecated by its authors. The README points training code to dlomix, the current models to Koina, and spectral library generation and rescoring to Oktoberfest and the Prosit website. The pretrained HCD fragmentation and iRT models are on figshare, as directories holding model.yml, config.yml and weights files named weights_{epoch}_{loss}.hdf5. A result should say which model directory was used and from where, because the repository itself holds no weights; this page read the repository at commit 6de9fea8.

sections.title: How the benchmark used it
sections.body: PepSpecBench describes Prosit as a GRU encoder-decoder of about 2.5M parameters and groups it with the sequence-centric models that predict b and y ion intensities indexed by cleavage position and fragment charge. All six baselines were retrained on the benchmark data under backbone-disjoint splits, so that figure and those results describe the benchmark's retrained model rather than the figshare checkpoints.

All baselines are retrained on the benchmark data under the Backbone-Disjoint splits described above.

run_guide.summary: Start the Prosit server from the repository with a downloaded model directory and predict spectra for the example peptide list.
prerequisites: A CUDA GPU, as the README's hardware section requires.
Docker 17.05.0-ce, nvidia-docker 2.0.3 with CUDA 8.0 and CUDNN 6 or later, and make 4.1.
A fragmentation model directory and an iRT model directory, downloaded by hand from https://figshare.com/projects/Prosit/35582.
About 3GB of download for the Docker container, which the README says takes about 5 minutes in their tests.

steps.title: Start the server with a model
steps.explanation: The README's usage command. It builds and runs the container, loads the two model directories and serves on port 5000. Each model directory holds model.yml, config.yml and a weights file.

quotes.text: make server MODEL_SPECTRA=/path/to/fragmentation_model/ MODEL_IRT=/path/to/irt_model/
In the example GPU device 0 is used for computation. The default PORT is 5000.
- weights file(s) - that follow the template `weights_{epoch}_{loss}.hdf5`

steps.title: Predict the example peptides
steps.explanation: Posts the example peptide list that ships with the repository to the running server and asks for the generic output format. The msp and msms endpoints take the same request.

quotes.text: curl -F "peptides=@examples/peptidelist.csv" http://127.0.0.1:5000/predict/generic
The examples take about 4s to run.

outputs: A predicted spectral file in the requested format. The README says the expected .generic, .msp and .msms outputs are in the examples folder and that the example takes about 4 s.
